newsitem.title: KENYA: Parliament speaker's wife wounded, bodyguard killed.
newsitem.headline: Parliament speaker's wife wounded, bodyguard killed.

text.p: The wife of Burundi's parliament speaker was wounded and her bodyguard killed in a landmine explosion on Monday night, a journalist in the capital Bujumbura said on Tuesday.

The journalist with Studio Jambo, a media production outfit, told Reuters by telephone from Bujumbura that the attack on Marie-Claire Ndekumana took place at 11 p.m. (2100 GMT) in a locality inhabited by politicians from the opposition Frodebu party.

Marie-Claire is the wife of National Assembly speaker Leonce Ndekumana. The journalist said her bodyguard was instantly killed when their vehicle rolled over an anti-tank mine as she returned home after visiting friends.
The latest explosion came three days after eight soldiers and four civilians were killed in Burundi in a landmine explosion in Gihanga commune in the tiny country's Bubanza province.
In that attack, three soldiers including an officer and three civilians were also wounded.

More than 150,000 people, mostly civilians, have died in Burundi's civil war since October 1993, when the country's first freely-elected Hutu president Melchior Ndadaye was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.

The war pits Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army against the armed wing of the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy. Military leader Pierre Buyoya announced a pre-ceasefire agreement last month with CNDD.
